comment: Right-to-left correctness, enforced rather than reviewed. A physical CSS property is
invisible in English and obviously broken in Hebrew, which is the worst kind of bug to
leave to human vigilance. See ADR-003, MON-502 and GAP §3 G-45.
The rule used to look at string Literals only, which missed the normal way a React
component is written: `className={`flex ${busy ? 'ml-2' : ''}`}` is a TemplateElement, not
a Literal, and passed silently. It also had no opinion on transforms — `translate-x-*`
never mirrors and is the highest-probability real RTL bug in a board layout — nor on
inline styles, nor on scroll geometry.
This file is JSON rather than JS so that eslint.config.js and the Vitest test that proves
these selectors actually fire can read the exact same bytes. Anything genuinely
unavoidable (a physical transform inside an already-mirrored context) takes a visible
eslint-disable comment naming the reason, which is a review artefact rather than silence.

restrictions.message: Physical utility in a string. Use the logical form (ms/me, ps/pe, start/end, text-start/text-end, border-s/border-e, rounded-s/rounded-e, gap instead of space-x, origin/bg/object with an arbitrary logical value) so the layout mirrors in Hebrew.
Physical utility inside a template literal — the usual way a className is built, and the case the old rule missed entirely. Use the logical form so the layout mirrors in Hebrew.

scrollLeft/scrollRight is physical, and its sign is inverted under dir="rtl" in a way that differs between engines. Use scrollIntoView, or scrollTo with an offset derived from the element's inline-start edge.
Physical property in an inline style. Use the logical name: marginInlineStart, paddingInlineEnd, borderInlineStartWidth, insetInlineStart.
Physical property in an inline style. Use insetInlineStart/insetInlineEnd, or float: inline-start/inline-end.
